newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Switzerland's UBS announces restructuring, expects loss.
newsitem.headline: Switzerland's UBS announces restructuring, expects loss.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland, the nation's largest bank, Tuesday announced a restructuring plan for its domestic operations that will result in a special three-billion Swiss franc ($2.3 billion) charge and a group loss for 1996.

UBS said it expected the group net loss to amount to about half a billion francs ($776 million). The three-billion-franc charge was to cover the future development of credit risk in its domestic portfolio, which it said would result in a reduction of the group's equity capital.
It said a provision of 120 million francs ($93 million) would also be taken to cover restructuring costs in the group's Region Switzerland.

"After the measures have been implemented, group equity will amount to 21.5 billion Swiss francs ($16.7 billion) at the end of this year, compared with 23 billion ($17.8 billion) at the end of 1995," UBS Chief Executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said in the text of a speech prepared for a news conference.

The restructuring calls for the bank to reduce the number of so-called domestic economic areas to eight from the current 31. UBS also anticipates the elimination of some 800 domestic jobs as a result of the restructuring.
As a result of the restructuring, UBS said it expected incremental earnings of 200 million francs ($155 million) a year from 1998 onward.

In addition, UBS said that as a result of the planned measures, Standard & Poor's had put the group on its Credit Watch List. However, Moody's Investor Service and IBCA, the European credit rating agency, have maintained their long-term AAA ratings on the groups.
